title: Evening lace shawl
subtitle: A triangle in lace-weight yarn with a repeating five-treble fan separated by chain spaces
excerpt: This triangular shawl uses a fan-and-shell lace pattern worked from the top down in lace-weight yarn on a 2.5 mm hook. Each fan is five trebles fanned into a ch-2 space, separated by chain arches from the previous row. Finished size is approximately 145 cm wide by 65 cm deep. The pattern is adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet (1886).
sourceNotes: Fan-and-shell lace triangle adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1886), 'A Shawl in Crochet Lace', Internet Archive scan. Stitch proportions updated for lace-weight yarn; original used 3-ply wool.
heroPrompt: A delicate triangular crochet lace shawl in ivory lace-weight yarn, spread on a dark velvet surface, showing the fan-and-shell lace repeat clearly from above, photographed in raking light.

glossaryTerms.definition: A group of treble stitches (here, five) all worked into the same chain space, fanning outward to form a shell or fan shape. The chain spaces between fans on the row below anchor each new fan.
A length of chains bridging two anchor points in lace crochet, forming an arch or loop. In this pattern, ch-5 arches separate the fans on alternate rows.
A finishing technique where small loops of chain are joined with a slip stitch to form decorative points along the border of a piece.

content.text: This triangular shawl uses a fan-and-shell lace pattern adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet. The construction is top-down, starting from a short chain at the neck point. Each lace row builds five-treble fans into the chain arches of the row below, with chain spaces between each fan forming the arches for the next row. The work is advanced because the lace repeat must remain aligned across increasing row widths, and because lace-weight yarn on a small hook requires attention to tension throughout.
A
fan stitch
here is five trebles all worked into the same ch-2 space. The fans sit above
chain arches
from the row below, and new arches form in the spaces between the fans on each row. The shawl finishes with a
picot edge
along the two diagonal sides. Blocking is essential: unblocked lace-weight crochet reads as a crumpled mesh; pinned and dried to the full dimensions it opens into clean lace.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 350 g lace-weight yarn (approximately 800 m per 100 g). A 2.5 mm crochet hook (US B/1 or C/2). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers (2). Blocking mat. Blocking pins (at least 60). Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

One fan repeat (5 tr + 2 ch-2 spaces) = approximately 3 cm wide; 6 fan rows = 5 cm deep in lace-weight yarn with a 2.5 mm hook, measured after light blocking. Gauge matters most for finished width: each fan repeat is 3 cm, and the final row has 48 fan repeats.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
fan stitch (5 tr into the same space).
picot (ch 3, sl st into base of chain).
Pattern

The shawl grows top-down. Each lace row adds one fan repeat on each side of the central spine, increasing the width by two fans per row. The spine is marked on every row. Work the pattern rows until the desired depth, then work the picot border along both diagonal edges.
Foundation
Ch 8. Sl st to first ch to form a small ring.
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 5 (counts as 1 tr + ch 2). [5 tr, ch 2, 5 tr] into ring (centre fan group). Ch 2, 1 tr into ring. Turn. (2 fans, 1 spine tr)
Row 2 (arch row)

Ch 3 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc into the first ch-2 space. Ch 5, 1 dc into the ch-2 spine space. Ch 5, 1 dc into the last ch-2 space. Ch 3, sl st to base tr to close. Turn. (2 ch-5 arches, 2 ch-3 edge arches)
Row 3 (fan row)

Ch 5 (counts as 1 tr + ch 2). 5 tr into first ch-3 edge arch. Ch 2, 5 tr into first ch-5 arch (fan A). Ch 2, [5 tr, ch 2, 5 tr] into spine arch (centre fan group, spine). Ch 2, 5 tr into second ch-5 arch (fan B). Ch 2, 5 tr into last ch-3 edge arch. Ch 2, 1 tr into sl st. Turn. (4 fans + 1 centre fan group = 6 fans)
Rows 4 to 48: continue fan and arch alternation

Continue alternating arch rows (even rows) and fan rows (odd rows). On each fan row, add one new fan on each side of the centre spine fan group by working a fan into each edge arch and each new ch-5 arch. On each arch row, work ch 5 between every adjacent fan's ch-2 spaces and ch 5 on each side of the spine ch-2 space. By row 48, the lower edge has 48 fans. The total stitch count in the final fan row is approximately 288 trebles within fans, plus chain spaces.
Picot border

Join yarn at the top right corner. Work along the right diagonal edge as follows: *1 dc into the ch-2 space of the edge tr/fan, ch 3, sl st into the base of the ch-3 just made (picot formed), 1 dc into the next ch-2 space or arch*; repeat from * to * along the full right diagonal edge. At the bottom point, work [1 dc, ch 3, sl st, 1 dc] into the lowest spine space. Continue the picot repeat up the left diagonal edge to the top left corner. Fasten off.
Finishing

Weave in all ends carefully through the backs of solid parts of the lace (not through chain spaces). Wet-block by soaking in cool water with a small amount of wool wash or fabric conditioner, gently squeezing to saturate without twisting. Press excess water out in a clean towel. Pin to 145 x 65 cm on a blocking mat: pin the two top corners first, then the bottom point, then the two diagonal edges at 5 cm intervals, easing each fan point outward. Leave until completely dry before unpinning.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Do not rub, wring, or tumble-dry. Press gently in a towel and lay flat to dry. Re-pin lightly if the lace loses shape after washing.
What to try next

Work the same fan-and-arch structure in fingering-weight yarn on a 3 mm hook for a slightly more robust lace fabric with a similar drape. Add a second picot row for a more elaborate border. The same fan repeat works as a rectangular stole if you cast on for the full width and work straight rows without spine increases.
